title: Night of the Living Dead
tagline: Board up the windows. Stock up the snacks.
about: Strangers barricade themselves in a farmhouse as the dead rise.
cue: Serve the snacks when everyone boards up the windows.
faces: “You can be the boss down there. I'm boss up here.”

Pennsylvania Farmhouse PantryNight of the Living DeadBoard up the windows. Bring the snacks.Every recipe serves 4.
    Cupboard SnacksUpstairs MainsPantry SweetsLong Night Drinks
    Cupboard SnacksBarbra's cemetery sandwichesEgg and cress, ham and mustard on white, crusts off, they're coming to get youHow to make it2 eggs20g mayonnaise10g cress, chopped8 slices of white bread25g butter, softened80g leg ham10g Dijon mustardBoil the eggs, cool, peel and mash with the mayonnaise.Stir in the cress.Butter the bread.Make two egg-and-cress sandwiches and two ham and mustard sandwiches.Trim the crusts and cut each sandwich into four small pieces.Wrap in baking paper for a 1968-style picnic.Black and white popcornBlack and white like the film stock. The blood on set was chocolate syrupHow to make it60g popcorn kernels1 tbsp neutral oil30g butter, melted1/4 tsp fine salt1/4 tsp cracked black pepper10g black sesame seedsPop the kernels in the oil in a covered pot over medium heat, shaking regularly, then divide in half.Toss one half with half the butter and the salt.Toss the other half with the remaining butter, pepper and black sesame seeds.Arrange side by side in a shared bowl.Farmhouse sardine and cheddar crackersSaltines with lemony mashed tinned fish, sharp cheese and pickled onion, as the boards go upHow to make itNot on tonight's cookSaltine crackers piled with tinned sardines mashed with lemon and parsley, sharp cheddar, and a quick pickled red onion, laid out on a chopping board.Thinly slice 1 red onion and soak it in 80ml white vinegar with 1 tsp sugar and a pinch of salt for 20 minutes.Drain 2 x 110g tins sardines and mash lightly with the juice of half a lemon, chopped parsley and pepper.Slice 150g sharp cheddar.Top 24 saltine crackers with sardine, a slice of cheddar and a few pickled onion rings and lay them out on a chopping board.Fried bologna on white breadThey're coming to get you, Barbra. Eat first.How to make itA house standard, not part of tonight's cook.Upstairs MainsCellar or upstairs farmhouse stewBeef chuck browned and braised slow with onion, carrot, potato, stock and thymeHow to make it800g beef chuck, cut into chunks1/2 tsp salt1/4 tsp black pepper1 tbsp neutral oil1 brown onion, chopped2 carrots, chopped500g potatoes, in chunks500ml beef stock4 thyme sprigs200g crusty Italian breadCut the beef and season it.Brown in batches in the oil in a heavy casserole.Add the onion, carrots, potatoes, stock and thyme.Cover and braise at 160°C, stirring once, until the beef is tender.Serve with crusty bread for soaking up the stock.Ben's beef and bean chilli with cornbreadMince simmered with cumin and kidney beans over sour cream and cheddar, hot buttered cornbreadHow to make itNot on tonight's cookBeef mince chilli simmered with cumin, chilli and kidney beans, ladled into bowls over sour cream and cheddar, with hot buttered cornbread on the side.Brown 700g beef mince in batches.Cook 1 diced onion and 3 garlic cloves 5 minutes, add 2 tsp cumin, 2 tsp chilli powder and 1 tsp smoked paprika, then 2 x 400g tins tomatoes and 400g drained kidney beans.Simmer 45 minutes.Mix 150g cornmeal, 100g plain flour, 2 tsp baking powder, 300ml buttermilk, 1 egg and 60g melted butter, pour into a hot buttered pan and bake at 220°C for 20 minutes.Serve with sour cream and cheddar.Pantry SweetsPantry peach cobbler with creamTinned peaches under a cinnamon scone top. Nobody goes down to the cellar for creamHow to make it1.7kg tinned peach halves (2 tins)1 tbsp cornflour80g cold butter200g self-raising flour60g caster sugar1 tsp ground cinnamon120ml milk1 tbsp raw sugar300ml pouring creamDrain the peaches, keeping a little syrup, and toss with the syrup and cornflour in a baking dish.Rub the butter into the flour, sugar and cinnamon, then mix in the milk to a soft dough.Drop spoonfuls over the peaches and sprinkle with raw sugar.Bake at 190°C until golden.Serve warm with cream.Long Night DrinksLong night spiked percolator coffeeStrong stovetop brew with brown sugar and Irish whiskey, lightly whipped cream floated on topHow to make it800ml strong brewed coffee2 tsp brown sugar120ml Irish whiskey150ml thickened creamBrew the coffee in a stovetop pot or plunger.Warm four heatproof glasses with hot water and tip it out.Put sugar and whiskey in each glass, add hot coffee and stir.Whip the cream until just pourable and float over the back of a spoon. Skip the whiskey for anyone who wants it plain.Cloudy farmhouse lemonadeCold drink for the long night, boards still going up.How to make itA house standard, not part of tonight's cook.
